name: Proof of Work
tagline: Security purchased with electricity and time.
overview: Validators (miners) compete to solve a computationally expensive puzzle. The first to solve it proposes the next block and earns the reward.
mechanism: Miners repeatedly hash block data with a changing nonce until the output falls below a target difficulty. Solving the puzzle is hard; verifying the solution is trivial for every other node.
advantages: Battle-tested security over 15+ years
No stake concentration required to participate
Highly resistant to Sybil attacks via real-world cost
workflow: Nodes broadcast pending transactions to the mempool
Miners assemble a candidate block from pending transactions
Miners iterate a nonce searching for a hash below the difficulty target
First valid solution is broadcast to the network
Peers verify the solution and extend their chain
Block reward and fees are paid to the winning miner

security.attack51: High cost, requires majority hash power

name: Proof of Stake
tagline: Security backed by capital at risk, not hardware.
overview: Validators lock up (stake) native tokens as collateral. The protocol selects a validator to propose each block, weighted by stake size.
mechanism: A pseudo-random algorithm selects a validator proportional to their stake. Validators who act maliciously have a portion of their stake destroyed (slashed).
advantages: Dramatically lower energy consumption than PoW
Faster block times and higher throughput
Economic penalties (slashing) discourage misbehavior
disadvantages: Wealth concentration can influence validator selection
workflow: Validators lock native tokens into a staking contract
Protocol pseudo-randomly selects a block proposer by stake weight
Proposer builds and broadcasts a candidate block
Other validators attest to the block's validity
Block finalizes once attestation quorum is reached
Rewards distributed; malicious behavior is slashed

name: Delegated Proof of Stake
tagline: Token holders elect a small council of block producers.
overview: Token holders vote for a limited set of delegates who take turns producing blocks, trading some decentralization for speed.
mechanism: Stakeholders cast votes weighted by holdings to elect a fixed number of delegates. Elected delegates round-robin block production and can be voted out.
advantages: Very high throughput and fast confirmation
Democratic accountability via continuous voting
Low hardware requirements for participants
workflow: Token holders vote to elect a fixed set of delegates
Elected delegates are scheduled in a round-robin production order
Each delegate produces a block during its assigned slot
Peers validate and append the block to the chain
Underperforming delegates can be voted out at any time
Rewards are distributed to delegates and often shared with voters

name: Proof of Authority
tagline: Reputation-vetted validators, tuned for private networks.
overview: A small set of pre-approved, identity-verified validators take turns producing blocks, prioritizing speed and predictability over decentralization.
mechanism: Validators are whitelisted based on verified identity and reputation. They sign blocks in a known rotation; misbehavior damages their public reputation.
advantages: Extremely fast and predictable block times
Low computational overhead
Well suited for consortium and enterprise chains
workflow: A governing body approves and whitelists validator identities
Validators are assigned a deterministic signing rotation
The scheduled validator signs and broadcasts the next block
Other authorities verify the signature and identity
Chain extends immediately with high confidence
Misbehaving authorities can be removed by governance vote

name: Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance
tagline: Vote your way to agreement, even with liars in the room.
overview: A known set of nodes exchange multiple rounds of signed messages to reach agreement, tolerating up to one-third faulty or malicious nodes.
mechanism: A leader proposes a value; nodes broadcast pre-prepare, prepare, and commit messages until two-thirds agree, achieving immediate finality.
advantages: Instant, deterministic finality
No forking - one canonical history
Well understood formal guarantees
disadvantages: Communication overhead scales quadratically with nodes
Impractical for very large validator sets
workflow: A leader node proposes a candidate block (pre-prepare)
Nodes broadcast 'prepare' messages to all peers
Nodes wait for 2f+1 matching prepare messages
Nodes broadcast 'commit' messages once prepared
Block commits once 2f+1 commit messages are collected
Result is final immediately, with no possibility of rollback

name: Tendermint BFT
tagline: PBFT reborn for public, stake-weighted networks.
overview: A round-based BFT protocol combining PoS validator sets with PBFT-style voting rounds, giving public chains instant finality.
mechanism: A proposer is chosen each round by stake weight; validators vote in propose, pre-vote, and pre-commit phases until two-thirds agree.
advantages: Instant finality with no forks
Combines open participation with fast consensus
Modular consensus engine (used across many chains)
disadvantages: Throughput bound by validator count and network latency
Validator set typically capped for performance
Liveness can stall if 1/3+ validators go offline
workflow: Round-robin proposer is selected by stake weight
Proposer broadcasts a candidate block
Validators pre-vote on the proposal
Validators pre-commit once 2/3 pre-votes are observed
Block commits once 2/3 pre-commits are collected
Chain advances to the next round with a new proposer

security.attack51: Requires 1/3+ stake to halt, 2/3 to corrupt

name: Avalanche Consensus
tagline: Agreement by repeated random sampling, not global voting.
overview: Nodes repeatedly sample small random subsets of peers and adopt the majority preference, converging on consensus probabilistically but rapidly.
mechanism: Each node queries k random validators about a transaction; if a strong majority agrees, confidence increases. Repeated sub-sampling rounds converge to near-certain finality within seconds.
advantages: Sub-second finality at large validator scale
High throughput without heavy communication overhead
Thousands of validators can participate
disadvantages: Newer design with a shorter security track record
Probabilistic safety rather than classical BFT proofs
workflow: A node receives a new transaction and forms an initial preference
The node queries k randomly sampled validators for their preference
If a supermajority agrees, the node's confidence increases
The sampling round repeats with new random subsets
Confidence accumulates until a finality threshold is crossed
Transaction is accepted as final across the network

name: Proof of History
tagline: A cryptographic clock that timestamps itself.
overview: A verifiable delay function generates a sequential hash chain that proves time has passed, letting validators order events before consensus even begins.
mechanism: A leader continuously hashes its own output, creating a verifiable sequence of time. This timeline is combined with a PoS-style voting layer (e.g. Tower BFT) to finalize blocks.
advantages: Removes the need to negotiate transaction order via messaging
Enables extremely high theoretical throughput
Pairs well with stake-weighted voting for fast finality
disadvantages: Requires powerful hardware to keep up with the hash chain
Historically prone to network instability under load
Relies on a small set of high-performance leaders
workflow: The current leader continuously hashes its own prior output
Transactions are timestamped by insertion into the hash sequence
The sequence is broadcast as a verifiable proof of elapsed time
Validators replay the hash chain to confirm ordering
A stake-weighted voting layer finalizes the ordered blocks
Leadership rotates on a fixed schedule

name: Proof of Capacity
tagline: Disk space stands in for computational brute force.
overview: Also known as Proof of Space, participants pre-compute and store large data plots on disk. Block rights go to whoever holds a matching plot closest to a target.
mechanism: Miners 'plot' hard drives with precomputed hash solutions ahead of time. When a challenge is issued, miners scan their plots for the closest matching value.
advantages: Far lower energy use than hash-power mining
Repurposes idle storage hardware
Discourages ASIC-style centralization
disadvantages: Plotting phase is disk-intensive and slow
Storage hardware wear and capacity arms races
workflow: Miners generate large plot files of precomputed hashes
Plots are stored on disk ahead of time
The network issues a random challenge
Miners scan their plots for the closest matching value
The closest match wins the right to produce the next block
Block is broadcast and verified by peers

name: Proof of Burn
tagline: Destroy coins today to earn mining rights tomorrow.
overview: Participants send tokens to a verifiably unspendable address, 'burning' them. The burned amount grants virtual mining power proportional to the sacrifice.
mechanism: Coins are sent to an eater address with no known private key. The protocol treats burned value as a proxy for long-term commitment, weighting block rights accordingly.
advantages: No ongoing energy expenditure after the burn
Aligns incentives toward long-term network health
Can bootstrap a new chain using an existing asset
disadvantages: Permanently destroys capital, which is economically wasteful
workflow: A participant sends tokens to a verifiably unspendable burn address
The burn transaction is recorded permanently on-chain
The protocol calculates virtual mining power from burned value
Burned power decays over time, requiring re-burning
Participants with the highest active burn win block rights
New blocks are broadcast and verified like any other chain

name: Proof of Elapsed Time
tagline: A trusted lottery run inside secure hardware.
overview: Each participant requests a randomized wait time from a trusted execution environment (TEE). Whoever's timer expires first wins the right to produce a block.
mechanism: A TEE (e.g. Intel SGX) generates a fair, verifiable random wait for each node. Hardware attestation proves the wait wasn't manipulated, keeping the lottery fair without brute-force computation.
advantages: Minimal energy consumption compared to PoW
Fair leader election without heavy computation
Well suited to permissioned enterprise consortia
disadvantages: Limited applicability to fully public networks
workflow: Each participating node requests a random wait time from its TEE
The TEE issues a signed, attested wait duration
Nodes idle until their individual timer expires
The first node whose timer expires broadcasts a new block
Peers verify the hardware attestation and timer proof
The chain extends and the lottery resets for the next block

name: Hybrid PoW + PoS
overview: Combines PoW block production with a PoS-based checkpointing layer, using staked validators to periodically finalize and secure the mined chain.
mechanism: Miners continue proposing blocks via PoW as usual, while a separate set of staked validators periodically vote to checkpoint the chain, making deep reorganizations economically irrational.
advantages: Retains PoW's permissionless block production
Adds PoS-style finality to limit reorg depth
Smooths the transition path between consensus models
disadvantages: Increased protocol complexity across two systems
Coordination overhead between miners and stakers
workflow: Miners compete via Proof of Work to produce new blocks
The mined chain grows as usual, block after block
Staked validators periodically convene to vote on a checkpoint
A checkpoint finalizes once a stake-weighted quorum agrees
Reorganizations beneath a finalized checkpoint are rejected
The cycle repeats at the next checkpoint interval

security.attack51: Requires majority hash power AND stake
